$comment: M189a (D974): one verdict per reached survivor of the census's runtime mutants, held to tflw-acceptance/mutation/reach.json by `npm run verify:reach-verdicts` in both directions. `not-asserted` = a plant runs through it and its known answer does not depend on the result (the dogfood is shallow there; a row is filed per family in testFlow/REVIEW_FINDINGS.md). `out-of-reach-by-design` = the result is visible only where the acceptance roster does not look, or is graded by a reference gate the census does not run (D751, D846). Read 2026-09-13 against the reach measured the same day over 106 plants at tflw main@29dfa0a. Re-read 2026-09-14 against `M190`'s re-census (the same 106 plants, tflw main@46750a0): 42 reached survivors again, 41 verdicts carried unchanged and one added (`threshold-scope-falls-back-to-the-whole-histogram`, added to the registry after the previous census and reached in this one).

ambiguity-count-from-a-second-query.why: the unmutated message reports the length of the list it is about to print and the mutant reports the count the step observed; the two differ only on a DOM that changed between the step's `.count()` and the single describing query — microseconds apart inside one failure path, with no gesture in between, so a fixture staging it would make its own known answer a race, and the unmutated code already has a named branch for that race. Measured rather than argued: applied to tflw on `fedora-box` 2026-09-15 with `M198` S3's whole plant in place — twelve matches, five shown, discriminators and all — the grader stayed green, 0 red lines. `M198` S3's ten legs kill the other nine.
ambiguity-count-from-a-second-query.was: the ambiguity message when a locator matches several elements: ten plants run through the formatter on a page where the locator was unambiguous, so the count and the list are never read; a plant would need a deliberately ambiguous locator and read the sentence back

ambiguity-list-without-discriminators.why: twelve `Retire` buttons with one distinct label between them: the grader requires every shown candidate to carry a discriminator and all of them to differ; computed and then not printed, the list is N identical quoted strings carrying zero bits for the choice it demands the reader make
ambiguity-list-without-discriminators.redLine: ✗ C13 recall — twelve identical `Retire` buttons are listed with what tells them apart (0/5 candidate(s), 0 distinct discriminator(s)) — computed and then not printed, the list is N identical quoted strings carrying zero bits for the choice it demands (`ambiguity-list-without-discriminators`)
ambiguity-list-without-discriminators.was: the per-candidate discriminator in the ambiguity list — same ten plants, same unambiguous pages; no known answer here has ever been a sentence about several matches

api-wait-ignores-its-own-budget.why: C67, C70, C71 and C72 run through the api-side budget line; C72 (`step:wait`) asserts the wait re-issues until its condition holds and stops — never that a `timeout wait` clause is the number that bounded it
api-wait-ignores-its-own-budget.redLine: the unsatisfiable wait named the step's own budget ("timed out after 30000ms (100 attempts): expected status to equal 200, but got 503")

applicability-collapses-to-pass.why: reached by C80's security assertion; rule applicability and the counts line are the security reference gates' subject (C57, verify:security-acceptance, D751)

array-body-flattened-to-an-object.why: `singletons.tflw` posts `[{…},{…}]` to `/subjects/echo`, which returns the bytes it received, and `body text` reads them back as the array; spread into an object the same body leaves as `{"0":…}` and both clauses go red
array-body-flattened-to-an-object.redLine: ✗ C67 recall — the bytes that left are the array itself — `[{"name":"Widget"},{"name":"Sprocket"}]` — where a body spread into an object leaves as `{"0":{…},"1":{…}}` (`array-body-flattened-to-an-object`)
array-body-flattened-to-an-object.was: 48 plants serialise an inline body here and none of them writes an array body, so the spread into an object never has an array to flatten; the wire is where it shows and the arrival server can echo a body

assertion-diagnosis-never-fires.why: `locator-diagnosis.tflw`'s first test misses on `button "Save drarft"` through `expect`, not through an action, and the grader reads the nearest-matches list out of the failure text; fired on actions only, the `expect` says nothing but "no matching element" while the identical `click` names the real button
assertion-diagnosis-never-fires.redLine: ✗ C13 recall — a miss on `button "Save drarft"` names the real button (NO LIST) — fired on actions only, the identical `click` names it and the `expect` says nothing but "no matching element" (`assertion-diagnosis-never-fires`)
assertion-diagnosis-never-fires.was: the nearest-matches diagnosis on a locator that resolved to nothing: every browser plant runs through it and reads the element that answered, never the sentence a miss produces; C13-C22 grade which element answered, C108 grades which web base a file is at home under

backoff-hold-kind.why: a module-level constant every plant loads; the D17 back-off diagnostic it names lands in the report as `backOff`, and C45 (`step:hold`) grades the arrival curve, not whether the run reported backing off — a `hold N users` against a path slow enough to back off is the fixture

blocked-port-hint-reads-undicis-prose.why: C6, C7, C95, C106 and C107 all pass through the hint; the mutant gates it on undici's own `bad port` text, which is what undici says today, so the two builds print the same sentence — the difference exists only under a future undici, which no fixture can install

browser-close-rethrow.why: 35 plants close a browser through these two lines and every launch succeeded; the mutant differs only after a launch failure, and its difference is the process exit status — neither is something an acceptance plant provokes or reads

comparison-coerces-operands.why: four tests written to fail hand `is less than` a boolean, `null`, a numeric string and a one-element array, each graded on the sentence naming what it got; coerced, all four pass (four clauses red)
comparison-coerces-operands.redLine: ✗ C65 recall — `is less than` refuses boolean by name (got ok=true: no error) — coerced with `Number()` it would compare as 1 and pass (`comparison-coerces-operands`)
comparison-coerces-operands.was: 37 plants compare with `is less than`/`is greater than` and every operand is a number, so the guard against `null`/`false`/`[]` is executed and never tripped; C60-C66 grade the seven matchers on values that fit them

config-files-resolve-against-cwd.why: M198 S1: no invocation can separate the two directories — `checkConfigFiles` has one call site (`cli.ts`, `configDir: cwd`) and the CLI reads `tflw.config` from `join(cwd, 'tflw.config')` with no `--config`/`--cwd` flag, so `resolve(configDir, …)` and `resolve(process.cwd(), …)` are the same path on every path in; the entry is killed by a unit test that injects a `configDir`, and it guards a flag tflw does not have. A plant would need the flag first
config-files-resolve-against-cwd.was: 79 plants resolve config file references and every grader runs `tflw` with its cwd at the config directory, where cwd-relative and config-relative are the same path; C106/C107 (`cert`/`key`) would need one run from elsewhere

csrf-attached-to-safe-methods.why: `session carrier` declares `csrf from body.csrfToken send as header`, and `sessions.tflw` issues one `GET` and one `POST` under it; `/__headers?name=x-csrf-token` on the arrival server says which arrival carried the token. Dropped, the verb condition sends it on the `GET` too — which no assertion inside the file can see, because both requests answer 200 either way
csrf-attached-to-safe-methods.redLine: ✗ C80 recall — and the `GET` carried none (saw ["csrf-6f1e"]) — a browser does not send one to a safe method and an application may reject it if it arrives, which is why the token has its own channel instead of joining a `header` step's (`csrf-attached-to-safe-methods`)
csrf-attached-to-safe-methods.was: 82 plants run through the CSRF attachment and none declares a session with a CSRF header, so the verb condition never has a token to withhold; the arrival server records request headers, so a session fixture against it can read the wire

diagnosis-ignores-the-resolved-element.why: `expect button "Publish release" is disabled` resolves the element and fails on its *state*, and the grader asserts the failure text carries no list at all; without the zero-match guard it is answered with the other buttons on the page — a diagnosis pointing away from the cause
diagnosis-ignores-the-resolved-element.redLine: ✗ C13 recall — a button that RESOLVED and failed on its state is answered about the state, not with a list of other buttons ("expected `button \"Publish release\"` to be disabled, but got (see above)\n  nearest matches ") — without the zero-match guard the diagnosis points away from the cause (`diagnosis-ignores-the-resolved-element`)
diagnosis-ignores-the-resolved-element.was: the nearest-matches diagnosis on a locator that resolved to nothing: every browser plant runs through it and reads the element that answered, never the sentence a miss produces; C13-C22 grade which element answered, C108 grades which web base a file is at home under

floor-filters-findings-not-rules.why: reached by C80's security assertion; the severity floor's denominator is graded by the security reference gates (D751)

imports-drop-body.why: 17 plants resolve imports through this line; what the dropped body costs is `TF044` across a file boundary, a check diagnostic, and check diagnostics are graded by C59's reference roster (verify-check-diagnostics), which the census does not run (D846)

input-stack-frame-raw-newline-only.why: a module-level pattern every plant loads; it fires on an input-probe finding, and input probing is graded by the security reference gates (C51-C58, verify:security-acceptance, D751), not by the acceptance roster

nearest-matches-not-deduped.why: `/diagnose-fixture` renders two buttons named `Save draft`, so the grader counts the lines that offer that suggestion and requires exactly one; offered again byte-identically, one string takes two of five candidate slots and the unnamed control is crowded out of the list entirely
nearest-matches-not-deduped.redLine: ✗ C13 recall — and names it exactly once for the two elements that render it (2 line(s)) — offered again byte-identically, one string takes two of five candidate slots and a genuinely different candidate cannot be shown at all (`nearest-matches-not-deduped`)
nearest-matches-not-deduped.was: the nearest-matches diagnosis on a locator that resolved to nothing: every browser plant runs through it and reads the element that answered, never the sentence a miss produces; C13-C22 grade which element answered, C108 grades which web base a file is at home under

oauth2-session-ctx.why: the same plant declares `as oauthLong`, so the `oauth2` arm is entered for the first time by any plant: its one reported step must carry `tflw.config`'s line 249. Handed the caller's raw context it prints nothing. This is the narrower of the pair — `session-source-lines` reddens both arms because the rebase is applied above the branch, and this one reddens only the `oauth2` clause, which is that structure stated as a measurement
oauth2-session-ctx.redLine: ✗ C80 recall — every one of the oauth2 session's 1 reported step(s) carries the text of its own line in `tflw.config` (0/1; first: line 249 reads "") — rendered from the caller's document instead, a line number past this 36-line file's end prints nothing at all (`oauth2-session-ctx`)
oauth2-session-ctx.was: C80 reaches the `if (decl.oauth2)` test and no plant declares an `oauth2` session, so the arm is never entered; whether apiV2 can serve one is the first question a plant here would have to answer

ok-ignores-no-verdict.why: 102 plants run through the report verdict and every run they read completed; `noVerdictReason` is non-null only for an aborted or inconclusive run, which no plant produces

open-model-agents-per-arrival.why: same eight plants, same curve-only grading — a fresh TCP handshake per arrival moves the reported latency and not the arrival count

open-model-back-to-fetch.why: eight perf plants run open-model arrivals through this line and grade the arrival curve the server recorded; none grades the reported latency, which is where the unpinned fetch path shows (p50 36 ms against 0 ms in the same process)

open-model-maxsockets-bounded.why: a module-level constant every plant loads; its effect — arrivals queuing inside the generator past 50 concurrent sockets and reporting the wait as service time — needs a workload that holds more than 50 connections open at once, and the perf plants are deliberately small (25 rps against a 50 ms path)

passing-assertion-gets-annotated.why: `expect button "Sprocket calibration" is hidden` *passes* — absence is the asserted state — and the grader reads that green step's own `detail`; appended regardless of outcome, a success reports "nearest matches on the page" stapled to it
passing-assertion-gets-annotated.redLine: ✗ C13 recall — an `is hidden` that passes on absence carries no diagnosis (ok=true, detail "`button \"Sprocket calibration\"` to be hidden\n  nearest matches on the ") — appended regardless of outcome, a green step reports success with "nearest matches" stapled to it (`passing-assertion-gets-annotated`)
passing-assertion-gets-annotated.was: the nearest-matches diagnosis on a locator that resolved to nothing: every browser plant runs through it and reads the element that answered, never the sentence a miss produces; C13-C22 grade which element answered, C108 grades which web base a file is at home under

request-headers-not-lowercased.why: reached by C80's security assertion; the rule that reads the lowercased header (`authenticated-response-cacheable`) is graded by the security reference gates (D751), and C80's own known answer is 200-with versus 401-without

reserved-scheme-passes-through.why: an absolute `api GET tflw://demoo/health` step — `TF071` reads only the config literal, so the runtime guard is the only refusal on this path — graded on the sentence naming the one legal spelling and on the arrival server having seen no `/health`; passed through it dies as `fetch failed`
reserved-scheme-passes-through.redLine: ✗ C97 recall — `api GET tflw://demoo/health` is refused by the sentence that names the only legal spelling (got ok=false: request failed: GET tflw://demoo/health — fetch failed) — passed through, it dies as `fetch failed` on an unknown protocol (`reserved-scheme-passes-through`)
reserved-scheme-passes-through.was: 82 plants pass their base URL through the reserved-scheme guard and every one is `http://`; a fixture whose `api` is a misspelt `tflw://` scheme, graded on the one-sentence refusal, is the plant

saturation-cpu-arm-never-fires.why: the generator self-diagnosis (`saturated`) is computed on every load run and lands in results.json; seven or eight perf plants read the arrival curve and never the diagnosis, and none of them drives its own generator hard enough to trip either arm — a deliberately saturating fixture is possible and expensive on a shared box

saturation-flips-a-gradable-threshold.why: reached by C3; the verdict-collapse it inverts needs a saturated generator, which no plant produces, so the merged `ok` is only ever computed over scenarios that all measured cleanly

saturation-ignores-the-min-window.why: the generator self-diagnosis (`saturated`) is computed on every load run and lands in results.json; seven or eight perf plants read the arrival curve and never the diagnosis, and none of them drives its own generator hard enough to trip either arm — a deliberately saturating fixture is possible and expensive on a shared box

saturation-lag-arm-never-fires.why: the generator self-diagnosis (`saturated`) is computed on every load run and lands in results.json; seven or eight perf plants read the arrival curve and never the diagnosis, and none of them drives its own generator hard enough to trip either arm — a deliberately saturating fixture is possible and expensive on a shared box

session-source-lines.why: `session-context.tflw` is 36 lines and names two sessions declared at `tflw.config` 195 and 249; the grader asserts every session step's reported `source` is the text at its own line in the config, and the plant's own steps against the plant. Without the rebase both arms render a config line number out of the caller's document and print the empty string
session-source-lines.redLine: ✗ C80 recall — every one of the hand-written session's 4 reported step(s) carries the text of its own line in `tflw.config` (0/4; first: line 195 reads "") — rendered from the caller's document instead, a line number past this 36-line file's end prints nothing at all (`session-source-lines`)
session-source-lines.was: C80 establishes a session and grades 200-with versus 401-without; the report `source` lines of the session steps — which document they were rendered from — are read by nothing

speculative-line-replaces-the-final-diag.why: 32 browser plants poll through this deadline and every one resolves inside ~3 s against a fast app, so a poll that gave up at the speculative mark is indistinguishable from one that kept going; a fixture with an element that appears at 5 s would tell them apart
speculative-line-replaces-the-final-diag.redLine: a locator that arrives at 5000 ms still resolved (ok=false) — and waited past the mark to do it (3216 ms)

spelled-out-duration-not-a-number.why: `expect duration is less than 2 seconds` on `/slow`, graded on the step passing and its detail reading `less than 2000`; with the conversion skipped the test errors with `got object`
spelled-out-duration-not-a-number.redLine: ✗ C65 recall — `expect duration is less than 2 seconds` compares as 2000 milliseconds (got ok=false: `is less than` expects a number, got object) — a duration left unconverted errors with `got object` (`spelled-out-duration-not-a-number`)
spelled-out-duration-not-a-number.was: same 37 plants, same numeric operands; `expect duration is less than 2 seconds` — the spelled-out form the unwrap exists for — appears in no fixture

suggestion-offered-without-its-ambiguity.why: the deduped `button "Save draft"` line must say that two elements render it; printed bare it looks like a clean, unique, ready-to-paste suggestion, and pasting it produces the *ambiguity* error — a different failure from the one being diagnosed
suggestion-offered-without-its-ambiguity.redLine: ✗ C13 recall — and the deduped line carries its own ambiguity ("- `button \"Save draft\"`") — SPEC §9.3 calls these ready-to-paste, and pasting this one produces the *ambiguity* error, a different failure from the one being diagnosed (`suggestion-offered-without-its-ambiguity-caveat`)
suggestion-offered-without-its-ambiguity.was: the nearest-matches diagnosis on a locator that resolved to nothing: every browser plant runs through it and reads the element that answered, never the sentence a miss produces; C13-C22 grade which element answered, C108 grades which web base a file is at home under

text-diagnosis-offers-structural-css-pat.why: a miss on `text "Inventroy reconciled"` must be answered with `text` suggestions only — `text`'s scan is `*` and a name is computed only for leaves, so the unnamed arm fired here answers with `css "html"`, `css "html > head"` and `css "html > body"`: structural containers in document order, one of which can never be visible
text-diagnosis-offers-structural-css-pat.redLine: ✗ C14 recall — and offers no structural container among its 5 suggestion(s) (2 `css "html…"`) — `text`'s scan is `*` and a name is computed only for leaves, so the unnamed arm fired here answers with `css "html"`, `css "html > head"` and `css "html > body"`: document order, one of which can never be visible (`text-diagnosis-offers-structural-css-paths`)
text-diagnosis-offers-structural-css-pat.was: the nearest-matches diagnosis on a locator that resolved to nothing: every browser plant runs through it and reads the element that answered, never the sentence a miss produces; C13-C22 grade which element answered, C108 grades which web base a file is at home under

threshold-scope-falls-back-to-the-whole-.why: the endpoint lookup behind `threshold … for "label"`: all eight workload plants (C3, C44–C50) evaluate thresholds through this line and none of them states a scoped one — C49's `verdict.tflw` grades an unscoped p95 and an unscoped error rate, so `scope === undefined` on every evaluation and the fallback to the whole histogram is the path the plant already takes; the only scoped threshold in either corpus is `perf/tflw/checkout-burst.tflw`, which the acceptance roster does not run. Not a candidate in the previous census — the `m172a` entry postdates it — so `M190`'s is its first measurement and this its first verdict. A plant would need a two-endpoint workload whose scoped p95 differs from the whole's

tls-facts-absent-counts-as-applicable.why: reached by C80's security assertion over plaintext; the TLS rules' applicability is graded by the security reference gates (D751), and C80 asserts nothing about the scan

ui-wait-ignores-its-own-budget.why: fifteen plants run the locator form of `wait until` and all of them are satisfied well inside both the step budget and the env budget, so which budget bounded the poll is never observed; the known answers are about what the wait waited FOR
ui-wait-ignores-its-own-budget.redLine: the locator form refused `for 3s` against this step's own 2 s budget ("") — the refusal is gone and the test passes

ungradable-threshold-passes.why: eight workload plants evaluate thresholds through this line and every one of them has successful iterations, so `actual === null` is never the case; C49 grades a red and a green threshold on a path that answers — a workload whose every request fails is the plant

unnamed-arm-dropped-for-every-kind.why: the fixture carries an icon-only button with no accessible name, and the grader requires a generated `css` path among the `button` miss's suggestions — it is a real candidate no name can reach, and dropping the arm removes it from the one list that could have named it
unnamed-arm-dropped-for-every-kind.redLine: ✗ C13 recall — and the icon-only button with no accessible name is surfaced as a generated CSS path — a real candidate no name can reach, dropped for every kind and it disappears from the one list that could have named it (`unnamed-arm-dropped-for-every-kind`)
unnamed-arm-dropped-for-every-kind.was: the nearest-matches diagnosis on a locator that resolved to nothing: every browser plant runs through it and reads the element that answered, never the sentence a miss produces; C13-C22 grade which element answered, C108 grades which web base a file is at home under

verdict-not-restamped-after-splice.why: reached only by C3 (`--workers 4` splices a merged report); the stale verdict needs an abort arriving at the splice, and no plant aborts a run — a plant that induces `inconclusive` under `--workers` is the missing fixture

wait-reader-picks-the-subject-over-the-r.why: the `wait until status of request to "…"` form: fifteen plants reach the reader and none of their fixtures writes the network-ref form, so the ordering of the two reads is never exercised; a browser fixture with `wait until … of request to` is the plant
wait-reader-picks-the-subject-over-the-r.redLine: the network-ref form of `wait until` polled observed traffic (ok=false) — at 116 ms against the page's 1200 ms probe

wait-until-diagnosis-dropped.why: the plant writes the same miss a second time as `wait until button "Save drarft" is visible` and the grader requires the timeout's text to carry the list too — the half of the fix a suite covering only `expect`/`check` would never notice was missing
wait-until-diagnosis-dropped.redLine: ✗ C13 recall — `wait until` carries the same diagnosis when it gives up (NO LIST) — the half of the fix a suite covering only `expect`/`check` would never notice was missing (`wait-until-diagnosis-dropped`)
wait-until-diagnosis-dropped.was: the nearest-matches diagnosis on a locator that resolved to nothing: every browser plant runs through it and reads the element that answered, never the sentence a miss produces; C13-C22 grade which element answered, C108 grades which web base a file is at home under
